audit.whatIsWrong: Chart rows 2, 5 and 6 read Sion while their own whys[] strings say 'Even at L3', 'You favour first item' and 'You favour 2+ items'.
audit.why: Packet chart is Tryndamere, Skill, Skill, Sion, Tryndamere, Tryndamere, Tryndamere over 1343 games at 52.2%. The sion__tryndamere mirror resolved its own split by moving onto the packet read as one atomic group; same resolution here.
audit.corrected: Row 2 to Skill, rows 5 and 6 to Tryndamere, as matched full/content pairs with ratings and reasons.

audit.whatIsWrong: No numbers, and Soul Furnace's 3-second detonation is nowhere.
audit.why: Decimating Smash 10/9/8/7/6, Soul Furnace 15/14/13/12/11 with a reactivation 3 seconds after the shield, Roar of the Slayer 12/11/10/9/8 at 800 range, Unstoppable Onslaught 140/100/60, Undying Rage 120/100/80. Sion's power curve is health-stacking, not armour-stacking, so your crit spike outpaces him rather than being blunted by resistances.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, mid and dontsFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Decimating Smash is written as if it always knocks up; Roar of the Slayer is written as plain poke; Glory in Death is described only as 'can still hit hard'.
audit.why: Riot's Decimating Smash text: 'If he charges for enough time, enemies hit by the swing will also be knocked up and stunned' — a quick release is damage only, and the wind-up length is the read. Riot's Roar of the Slayer text reduces the Armor of the first enemy hit and, on hitting a minion, knocks that minion back through everything in its path — so he can shove a creep into you. Riot's Glory in Death text: the reanimated attacks 'heal him and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health', which is why Grievous Wounds and not armour is the answer to the corpse phase.
audit.corrected: Charge condition, armour shred plus minion knockback, and the zombie's healing/max-health damage all stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'terrain-cuts-retreat' missing-interaction rule for this matchup is wrong on both halves.
audit.why: Riot's Unstoppable Onslaught text is a steerable charge that damages and knocks up on collision — it creates no terrain, and the kit's terrain flag is a tooltip-parse misfire. The rule also asserts Tryndamere 'has no dash'; Spinning Slash is a 650-range dash.
audit.corrected: Not written to the page. Flagged here so the rule is not re-applied.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Sion must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online — his charged Smash threatens, but Bloodlust keeps trades even. This stage is won by sidestepping the swing.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Decimating Smash's cooldown.
edits.after: Stridebreaker is your spike — crit shreds him faster than he stacks health, so force it on completion.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Sion carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: you out-DPS and out-split him — but walk away from the zombie instead of standing on the corpse.

edits.before: You favour first item — crit shreds him faster than he stacks armour and you can lock him with W.
edits.after: You favour first item — crit shreds him faster than he stacks health, and Mocking Shout keeps him near.

edits.before: You out-splitpush Sion easily, but respect his passive — killing him spawns a raging zombie that can still hit hard, so back off during the death timer and disengage his ultimate freight-train.
edits.after: You out-splitpush Sion easily, but respect Glory in Death — the zombie's attacks heal him and scale off your max health, so carry Grievous Wounds and walk away from the corpse instead of trading with it.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 Sion gets to threaten: a charged Decimating Smash (Q) into Roar of the Slayer (E) is a real chunk and can knock you up for his jungler. Sidestep the smash, wait out its cooldown, then trade with your heal advantage.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 Sion threatens: a charged Decimating Smash (Q) into Roar of the Slayer (E) chunks you, knocks you up for his jungler, and shreds your armour — and E knocks a minion back through you too. Sidestep the smash, then trade on its 10s.

edits.before: - Sion Decimating Smash: matchup-defining — Charged = knockup. Sidestep it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Decimating Smash: 10s at rank 1 — a full charge knocks up and stuns, a quick release does not, so read the wind-up length. - Soul Furnace shields, then detonates 3s later. - Undying Rage: 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Track Sion's Decimating Smash (Stun): Charged = knockup. Sidestep it. When it is down — Crit him down.
edits.after: Only a fully charged Decimating Smash knocks up — a quick release is damage you can walk through.

edits.before: Charged = knockup. Sidestep it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Decimating Smash is 10s — bait a quick release, then commit on the cooldown.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Soul Furnace detonates 3s after he shields — swing, then step out.

edits.before: That is Sion's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Roar of the Slayer knocks a minion through you and shreds your armour.

notes: The packet suspectName 'Use Unstoppable Onslaught' is a FALSE POSITIVE — correct name with a verb in front. The 'terrain-cuts-retreat' missing-interaction rule for this matchup is doubly wrong (R makes no terrain per Riot's text; Spinning Slash IS a dash) and I did not write it to the page. Whether Undying Rage's invulnerability holds you in place through a full-distance Unstoppable Onslaught knockup is not in this data — left alone.
